# A server action re-renders the whole page on the next GET, so a route's
# markup is written into the response and never patched. A conditional over
# mutable state asks for the opposite: the reactivity lowering turns it into a
# __renderSlotN that patches the DOM from the client.
#
# One package gets one lowering, so a build that needs both for the same window
# cannot have them. That is a gap, and what it used to do was panic inside the
# Go translator on `lower.CreateNode` -- an op no language registers an emitter
# for, and a stack trace rather than a diagnostic. It is refused by name now,
# and the refusal is what a fixture can hold until route mode can render such a
# window itself.

! sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out app.sngl
stderr 'route /p has a server-side action'
stderr 'cannot emit both for one window'
! exists out/server.go

-- go.mod --
module reactiveslot

go 1.24

-- srv/srv.go --
package srv

func Bump(n int) int { return n + 1 }

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import nav "sngl:ui/nav"
import "go:reactiveslot/srv"
import "sngl:platform/html"

var hits = 0

window(title=pages.current.title) {
    nav.stack #pages {
        nav.page #page(href="/p", title="t") {
            html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = srv.Bump(hits) })
            if hits > 0 {
                html.span(innerText="hit")
            }
        }
    }
}
